title: The Math of Paying Cash for a Car

beats.say: You think paying cash for a car saves you money, but the actual math on a $25,000 purchase proves you might be richer keeping the cash.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a solitary car parked on a rain-slick asphalt lot under cold sodium streetlights.

beats.say: Most people assume zero debt is always the smartest financial move.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a massive concrete highway overpass cutting through heavy blue hour fog.

beats.say: So why do certain buyers finance at 5% and keep their cash invested instead?
beats.visual: Close up of wet metal guardrails reflecting faint amber tailights in the dark.

beats.say: Because if you invest that $25,000 at 8% a year, compound growth changes the outcome completely.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a single tower edge stretching up into a cold winter night sky.

beats.say: Over 5 years, the loan interest costs you a few thousand dollars.
beats.visual: Extreme close up of water droplets sliding down a cold glass window at night.

beats.say: Yet your invested cash continues compounding at 8% a year over that same timeframe.
beats.visual: High angle shot of empty dark city streets lit by harsh fluorescent lights.

beats.say: That growth can outpace the total interest paid on the 5% car loan.
beats.visual: Wide shot of open water at dusk with dark grey ripples under a heavy grey sky.

beats.say: Keeping liquid cash gives you safety and earning power that sitting in a car's metal frame can't match.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a person walking across a vast concrete plaza under a massive bridge.

beats.say: You don't lose money to the dealer upfront, and your capital keeps working for you.
beats.visual: Close up of rusted iron bolts on a damp bridge beam in cold blue light.

beats.say: That's how smart buyers protect their wealth while still driving what they need.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a tall concrete stairwell lit by a single bare overhead bulb.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a lonely highway stretching infinitely into dark rolling hills.
